text:
Maya: Hey team, seeing weird scheduling after nodepool autoscale in us-west-2. New GPU nodes came up but most inference pods stayed Pending with toleration mismatch. :eyes:

Maya: kubectl describe node gpu-spot-abc shows taints:
```
key: gpu.isolation=dedicated:NoSchedule
```
But our pod tolerations expect `gpu-dedicated:NoSchedule` (old key).

Igor: Do we have a node init script that sets taint? I thought NodePool template uses `gpu-dedicated` key. Can you paste `kubectl get node -o jsonpath` for the node labels/annotations? :thinking:

Maya: here's output:
```
kubectl get node gpu-spot-abc -o jsonpath='{.spec.taints}'
[{"key":"gpu.isolation","value":"dedicated","effect":"NoSchedule"}]
```
Also node annotations show `cloud-init-version: 4.7` and `user-data-hash` changed.

Sophie: Likely culprit: new cloud-init/packer image changed how taints are written (dot vs dash). I saw similar when a bootstrap script used `kubectl taint nodes $NODE gpu.isolation=dedicated:NoSchedule` instead of `gpu-dedicated=dedicated:NoSchedule` after a distro update. That would bypass our admission controller.

Igor: Oof. cluster-autoscaler then scaled up target pool A (taint key A) while our pod nodeSelector/affinity points to pool B (taint key B) → pods Pending. Can we patch pods with tolerations temporarily? `kubectl patch deployment ... --type='json' -p ...` to add a toleration for gpu.isolation?

Kai: Cost note: we have ~12 nodes in warm pool and autoscaled 8 spot GPUs, running ~10 empty while pending pods starved. That costs ~$1.60/min roughly. Rolling fix preferred.

Maya: I'm going to add a one-off toleration to the inference deployment to get things running: `kubectl patch deployment inference -n prod --patch '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"tolerations":[{"key":"gpu.isolation","operator":"Equal","value":"dedicated","effect":"NoSchedule"}]}}}}'`

deploy-bot: nodepool/gpu-spot scaled from 3 to 11 (reason: unschedulable pods) <https://infra.internal/ops/scale-events/2101234567>

Sophie: After Maya's patch pods started scheduling. Next steps: 1) fix NodePool launch template to use canonical taint key `gpu-dedicated`. 2) Add admission webhook to normalize taint keys on join or reject nonconforming. 3) Run a rolling restart of NodePool so taints are re-applied.

Igor: Also add cluster-autoscaler filter to prefer NodePool by label instead of taint matching so we don't scale wrong family. We should also set `--expander=least-waste` and prefer the dedicated pool.

Kai: Agree. Also add a short runbook and cost estimate, +alert when >5 idle GPUs for >10m.

Maya: Will open PR for node image and an infra ticket. For now keep the temp toleration for 1 hour then revert. Thanks. :thumbsup:

Igor: FYI I see a second issue: kubelet on an older image sometimes writes taint key with underscore `gpu_isolation`. Let's search for that pattern across nodes: `kubectl get nodes -o json | jq '.items[].spec.taints' | grep gpu_` — might need to normalize.

Sophie: Good call. If multiple variants exist we should run a one-off script to retag taints: `for n in $(kubectl get nodes -l nodepool=gpu -o name); do kubectl taint nodes $n gpu.isolation-; kubectl taint nodes $n gpu-dedicated=dedicated:NoSchedule; done` — but be careful with eviction.

Maya: I'll coordinate during low traffic window. Logging ticket: INFRA-4372. Will ping @oncall if we hit evictions.

Kai: ping @oncall when you start. Also check spot termination notice for the 8 extra nodes so we don't lose work mid-fix.

Maya: starting patch now. update in 10m.
